stem:
Krish compares a hen with a goat after fertilisation. He asks where the fertilised egg develops into an embryo in each case.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: In the hen the fertilised egg is laid and the embryo develops during hatching; in the goat the embryo develops inside the female body until birth.
Bird and mammal mean the same thing here, so both embryos must develop only inside a laid egg.
The comparison holds even before fertilisation, so place of development does not depend on a fertilised egg.
Food and oxygen supply decide the place of development first, and that decides whether fertilisation happened.

teacher.key_rationale: Birds develop the embryo in a laid egg during hatching; most mammals develop the embryo inside the female until birth. Equating bird with mammal, dropping the after-fertilisation condition, or reversing supply and place of development miss the hinge.
